question: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has noted a significant increase in water temperatures in the Pacific since May 2026, with measurements exceeding the average by over 6 °C. According to the WMO, the El Niño climate phenomenon is 80 % likely to take place between June and August 2026, with a 90 % likelihood of lasting until November.

As stated by UN Secretary-General António Guterres, this is an urgent climate warning as there would be an increased chance of extreme weather events in the coming months and, therefore, an increased risk of extreme rainfall, floods, fires, heatwaves, intensified droughts and increased cyclone activity, both in Europe and around the world. Given this situation: 1.

What measures is the Commission taking to prevent, prepare for and respond to this potential El Niño episode, which may lead to an increase in natural disasters in Europe and around the world in the coming months?
Given the increased risk of fires, has the Commission extended the rescEU reserve, in line with the EU’s fire strategy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.8.2026) The Commission is actively monitoring the new El Niño phase, among others through Copernicus Climate Change Service1, by publishing reports on plausible scenarios and its impacts2, and stands ready to support any potentially affected country via the Union Civil Protection Mechanism (rescEU).

Flexible, early and anticipatory action is a critical element of effective crisis management. To support this approach, the humanitarian funding framework includes crisis modifiers (CM) which enable humanitarian partners to rapidly reallocate resources from ongoing actions to respond to newly emerging shocks.

It is designed to address immediate, life-saving needs arising from rapid-onset crises or deteriorating situations, particularly when no other response mechanisms are yet in place. The Emergency Response Coordination Centre mapped its ongoing humanitarian aid projects where CM might be activated to address new needs3.

In response to the increasing frequency and intensity of wildfires, the Commission created rescEU in 2019 and developed its aerial forest firefighting fleet. In 2023, the number of rescEU aerial firefighting assets was doubled.

In addition, grants have been awarded to six Member States for the procurement of 12 medium amphibious aircraft, which will become operational from 2028 onwards, and to three Member States for the procurement of five helicopters. The Commission promotes a holistic and integrated approach to wildfire risk management, as outlined in its recent Communication4 on the subject.

In line with the latter, the Commission intends to maintain the current level of ambition for the rescEU aerial firefighting fleet, while retaining the possibility of procuring additional aircrafts if needed.

1 https://climate.copernicus.eu/. 2 https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC147365. 3 Several CM have already been activated in response to El Niño, notably in Central America: The Commission

allocated of EUR 2.6 million to humanitarian partners to cover the basic food needs of more than 13 200 vulnerable individuals in Guatemala and Honduras. A crisis modifier was activated for a German Red Cross project in Guatemala. Around 250 families will receive a one-off cash transfer of USD 150 per household.

In Belize, the World Food Programme has activated drought anticipatory action payouts, delivering early cash assistance to 419 pre-identified rain-fed smallholder farmers for investment in drought-tolerant seeds and water storage during the pre-impact window, to reduce crop losses and safeguard livelihoods. 4 COM(2026) 330 final.
